sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Build, dev server and test settings
sections.what: Sets up the Vite build tool with React support. During development, any request starting with /api is passed on to a backend server at 127.0.0.1 port 8765. Tests run in a plain Node environment and only pick up files ending in .test.ts or .test.tsx under src.
sections.why: Likely reason: the proxy lets the browser talk to the backend without cross-site restrictions, and the base setting of ./ makes file paths relative so the built app can be opened from other folders.
sections.watch_out: If the backend is not running on port 8765, every /api call from the app will fail during development.

summary: Settings for building and serving the frontend. It sets up React, relative asset paths, inline small assets, a proxy from the frontend to the backend API, and test settings.
purpose: Controls how the frontend is built for release and how it runs in development.
why: Likely reason: a relative base path lets the built app run from whatever folder it is packaged in. The other choices are not explained in the code.
how: Vite reads these settings, builds the bundle with the React plugin, and during development forwards every request starting with /api to the backend.
inputs: Frontend source files and the backend running at 127.0.0.1 port 8765.
outputs: The built frontend bundle and the development server with its proxy.
risks: Source maps are turned off, so debugging the built app is harder. The bundle size warning limit is raised, which hides large bundles. The backend address is fixed in the file.
debug: If API calls fail during development, check that the backend runs on port 8765. If the packaged page is blank, check the base path.
